url: /mimus/tutorials/first-run.md
---
# Tutorial: your first audit

Goal: point mimus at a repo's docs and see which claims are still
true — docs-as-tests, in minutes.

## 1. Init

```sh
cd your-repo
mimus init
```

Writes a commented `mimus.toml` and a `rules/` dir. Defaults:

```toml
[sources]
docs = ["README.md", "docs/**/*.md", "AGENTS.md", "project/**/*.md"]
comments = true
cards = ".kuda/modules/*.yaml"

[check]
mechanical = true
semantic = false
```

## 2. Check

```sh
mimus check
```

Claim extraction scans every configured doc: backticked paths,
shell commands, symbol names, counts, links. Each claim is
verified against reality — the filesystem, PATH, the kuda index
(symbol claims need `kuda sync`; without an index they're
silence, not failures):

```
README.md:42 [error] `src/old_api.rs` — ./src/old_api.rs does not exist
docs/guide.md:17 [warn] `cargo bench` — binary `cargo-bench` not found in PATH
2 violation(s)
```

Exit code is `1` on any `error`-severity violation — docs drift
becomes a gateable signal.

## 3. Make a claim and watch it get caught

Add a line to your README referencing a file that does not exist:

```md
See `nonexistent/dead.rs` for the implementation.
```

```sh
mimus check
```

```
README.md:N [error] `nonexistent/dead.rs` — ./nonexistent/dead.rs does not exist
```

Every violation is claim + evidence + (when mechanical) a fix —
the evidence bar is the design rule, see
[architecture](../explanation/architecture.md).

## 4. Author a convention

`rules/` is data. Add `rules/no-todos.toml`:

```toml
name = "no-todos"
message = "TODO left in committed source"
severity = "warn"
files = "src/**/*.rs"

[match]
kind = "source-pattern"
pattern = "TODO|FIXME"
```

`mimus check` now flags every TODO — a convention encoded as a
file, not a code change. See [authoring rules](../how-to/rules-authoring.md).

## 5. Audit the memory layer

If the repo is kuda-indexed:

```sh
kuda sync && mimus audit
```

```
fresh        kuda-store
drifted      kuda-core
20 fresh, 1 drifted, 0 contradicted
```

Cards whose `verify:` files changed since sync report `drifted`;
missing files report `contradicted`.

## You have built

A falsification layer: every factual claim in your docs is now a
test that fails loudly when reality moves.

Next: [gate CI on it](../how-to/ci-gate.md),
[write rules](../how-to/rules-authoring.md).

# How-to: multi-repo checking

Docs in one repo make claims about sibling repos — moved crates,
`see ../<repo>`, cross-repo commands. mimus verifies those claims
where it can reach reality.

## Per-repo config

Each repo keeps its own `mimus.toml` and `rules/` — conventions
are repo-scoped (a rule that is right for `platform` is noise in
`lsp`). Run `mimus check` per repo, or script the sweep:

```sh
for r in ~/GitHub/handl-lang/*/; do
  [ -f "$r/mimus.toml" ] && (cd "$r" && mimus check)
done
```

## Cross-repo claims today

* **Paths** are resolved relative to the repo root — a
  ../sibling/crate claim in docs verifies if the sibling exists.
* **Commands** check PATH, which is host-global — a doc telling
  users to run `hnl` is verified wherever `hnl` is installed.
* **Symbols** need a kuda index per repo; the `symbol` checker
  reads `.kuda/index.sqlite` of the *current* root. Cross-repo
  symbol resolution rides on kuda workspace mode.

## Rules at scale

Keep org-wide conventions in one place and symlink or vendor
them per repo — a shared rules/org/ directory fetched in CI
works today; first-class rule inheritance is a backlog item.

## Where it goes next

`kuda sync --workspace` produces per-root indexes across the
sibling set; the `symbol` checker then resolves claims like
`` `hnl` lives in the cli repo`` against the merged stores —
the "which repo owns this" question becomes verifiable.

---

---
url: /mimus/how-to/kuda-audit.md
---
# How-to: audit kuda memory

`mimus audit` is the falsifier for the memory layer: it verifies
every `.kuda/modules/*.yaml` card against source — memory
audited, not just generated.

## Run

```sh
kuda sync        # (re)generate the index first
mimus audit
```

```
fresh        kuda-store
fresh        kuda-core
drifted      kuda-cli
20 fresh, 1 drifted, 0 contradicted
```

## Scores

| score          | meaning                                              |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `fresh`        | every `provenance.files` hash still matches          |
| `drifted`      | a verify file's content changed since sync           |
| `contradicted` | a provenance file no longer exists                   |

Audit recomputes git `hash-object` per `provenance.files` entry
and compares with what the card recorded at sync time — the same
provenance model `kuda status` uses, checked from the outside.

## Exit semantics

Audit is report-tier: exit `0` even with contradictions. It is
diagnosis, not a gate — pair it with `mimus check` if you want
drift to fail CI, or keep it in a scheduled report job. The fix
is upstream anyway: `kuda sync`, not a hand-edit.

## What it does not check (yet)

Audit verifies *freshness* (provenance hashes), not *accuracy*
of the card's prose fields — `api`/`deps` drift beyond their
recorded inputs, or a hand-written `notes:` that has gone stale,
is the semantic tier's job when it lands.

---

---
url: /mimus/how-to/rules-authoring.md
---
# How-to: author rules

Conventions live in `rules/*.toml` — data, not code. A new rule
is a new file; the engine vocabulary stays fixed. Rules run in
`mimus check` alongside the claim checkers.

## The format

```toml
name = "no-positional-dispatch"
message = "dispatch via lang.eval roles — never kind == shape checks"
severity = "error"          # error (gates check) | warn (report only)
files = "crates/plugin-engine-*/src/**/*.rs"

[match]
kind = "source-pattern"
pattern = 'kind\s*==\s*"(assign|block|paren|return)"'
```

| field      | meaning                                            |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`     | identifier — shown in output + rules listing       |
| `message`  | the *evidence* attached to each finding            |
| `severity` | `error` fails `mimus check`; `warn` reports        |
| `files`    | glob under the repo root                           |
| `[match]`  | `kind = "source-pattern"` + a regex                |

## Semantics

Every line matching `pattern` in every file matching `files`
becomes a `Behavior` violation carrying `message` as evidence.
Lines are matched individually — craft patterns for what a single
line can express.

## The evidence bar applies to rules too

A rule that cannot cite a specific line emits nothing — there is
no "file smells wrong" rule kind. And an invalid regex is not a
finding either: it is silence plus a `mimus doctor` complaint.
If your rule keeps flagging real code, the rule is wrong —
narrow the `files` glob or the pattern.

## Examples

Ban a deprecated API in a bound region:

```toml
[match]
kind = "source-pattern"
pattern = '\bold_api::'
```

`files = "crates/**/src/**/*.rs"` — one file, one convention,
reviewable in PRs like code.

Require README badges? That is a *presence* check — not what
`source-pattern` does; absence-of-pattern rules are a planned
`kind`, deliberately out until the evidence story is right.

## Verify

```sh
mimus check            # runs rules + claim checkers
mimus report --format json | jq '.[] | select(.claim.kind=="behavior")'
```

# How-to: gate CI on docs

`mimus check` is the mechanical tier — deterministic, offline,
safe to gate. Exit `1` when any `error`-severity violation
exists.

## The gate

```sh
mimus check
```

Wire it like a test: run in CI on every PR. Doc paths, commands,
symbols and your `rules/*.toml` conventions all gate the same
way.

## `--no-cmd` — never execute anything

The `cmd` checker verifies documented commands exist on PATH —
it does **not** run them. But if you want to be explicit that a
job runs nothing executable:

```sh
mimus check --no-cmd
```

`--no-cmd` skips the command checker entirely; path/symbol/rules
checks still run.

## Severity is the gate boundary

* `error` — mechanical, reproducible: dead paths, missing
  binaries, rule violations marked `severity = "error"`.
* `warn` — env-dependent or heuristic: shown in output and
  `--format json`, never fails the run.

Tune per rule in `rules/*.toml` (`severity = "warn"`).

## Report for humans

```sh
mimus report                    # always exits 0 — full list
mimus check --format json       # machine-readable for tooling
```

`report` is the audit-view command: same violations, never a
gate. `reconcile`-style tooling consumes the JSON.

## Recommended setup

```yaml
# whatever your CI is
- run: mimus check --no-cmd
```

Docs that can drift silently are docs that will. One line keeps
them honest.

### Gating only new drift (large backlogs)

`mimus check --diff <spec>` runs the same checkers but only over
claims in files matching `git diff --name-only <spec>` — PR
checks fail on *new* drift while the existing backlog is paid
down:

```yaml
- run: mimus check --diff "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}...HEAD"
```

`--diff` needs a git checkout — outside a repo it exits 2.

See [claims & tiers](../explanation/claims.md) for why the
semantic tier can never be this gate.

# Command-Line Help for `mimus`

This document contains the help content for the `mimus` command-line program.

**Command Overview:**

* [`mimus`↴](#mimus)
* [`mimus init`↴](#mimus-init)
* [`mimus check`↴](#mimus-check)
* [`mimus fix`↴](#mimus-fix)
* [`mimus audit`↴](#mimus-audit)
* [`mimus report`↴](#mimus-report)
* [`mimus doctor`↴](#mimus-doctor)
* [`mimus coverage`↴](#mimus-coverage)
* [`mimus claims`↴](#mimus-claims)

## `mimus`

Spots the cuckoo eggs in your repo — claim verification: docs-as-tests, memory audit

**Usage:** `mimus [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `init` — Detect sources -> mimus.toml + rules/ scaffold
* `check` — Verify claims. Mechanical tier by default
* `fix` — Apply mechanical rewrites for confirmed violations
* `audit` — Trust-score .kuda/ cards vs source
* `report` — Full violations list with evidence
* `doctor` — Checker/config/kuda-index health
* `coverage` — Doc coverage — which indexed symbols no doc ever names. The reverse direction of `check`: code has it, docs silent
* `claims` — Dump extracted claims (kind/source/line) — tuning aid for the extractor's precision on real docs

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (else $MIMUS_CONFIG, ./mimus.toml, ~/.config/mimus/mimus.toml)
* `--format <FORMAT>` — Output format: human | json

  Default value: `human`

## `mimus init`

Detect sources -> mimus.toml + rules/ scaffold

**Usage:** `mimus init`

## `mimus check`

Verify claims. Mechanical tier by default

**Usage:** `mimus check [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--all` — Include the semantic tier (advisory only, never gates)
* `--no-cmd` — Skip command claims — the PATH probe is machine-dependent
* `--diff <SPEC>` — Only check claims in files matching `git diff` SPEC — e.g. `--diff origin/main...HEAD` gates a PR on new drift

## `mimus fix`

Apply mechanical rewrites for confirmed violations

**Usage:** `mimus fix [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--dry` — Show the plan, write nothing
* `--semantic` — Agentic tier: agent proposes corrected claim text for semantic (REFUTED) findings. Needs \[check].acp_cmd

## `mimus audit`

Trust-score .kuda/ cards vs source

**Usage:** `mimus audit`

## `mimus report`

Full violations list with evidence

**Usage:** `mimus report`

## `mimus doctor`

Checker/config/kuda-index health

**Usage:** `mimus doctor`

## `mimus coverage`

Doc coverage — which indexed symbols no doc ever names. The reverse direction of `check`: code has it, docs silent

**Usage:** `mimus coverage`

## `mimus claims`

Dump extracted claims (kind/source/line) — tuning aid for the extractor's precision on real docs

**Usage:** `mimus claims [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--all` — Include card-prose Behavior claims too

&#xA;This document was generated automatically by
clap-markdown.&#xA;

# Config — `mimus.toml`

## Top level

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sources` | `SourcesCfg` | optional | — |
| `check` | `CheckCfg` | optional | — |
| `rules` | `RulesCfg` | optional | — |
| `report` | `ReportCfg` | optional | — |

## `[sources]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs` | `list` | optional | Doc glob patterns mined for claims. |
| `comments` | `bool` | optional | Extract claims from code comments too. |
| `cards` | `string` | optional | Glob for memory cards to audit (empty = skip). |

## `[check]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mechanical` | `bool` | optional | Mechanical tier — deterministic, CI-gateable. |
| `semantic` | `bool` | optional | Semantic tier — advisory only, can never gate. |
| `kuda_index` | `path` | optional | kuda index path for the symbol checker. |
| `acp_cmd` | `string` | optional | ACP agent command for the semantic checker (e.g. "cline --acp"). Semantic tier is advisory only. |
| `base_dirs` | `Vec<PathBuf>` | optional | Extra repo-relative roots path claims resolve against — for docs that reference paths relative to a component root (e.g. "infrastructure/postgres"). |
| `kinds` | `Vec<ClaimKind>` | optional | Only check claims of these kinds (empty = all). |
| `ignore_prefixes` | `list` | optional | Skip claims whose text starts with any of these prefixes. |
| `binaries` | `list` | optional | Tool prerequisites the repo declares — commands invoking these skip the PATH probe (docs may legitimately require tools the checker's machine lacks). |

## `[rules]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `path` | optional | Dir of \*.toml rule files. |
| `strict` | `bool` | optional | Rule violations also fail `check` (not just report). |

## `[report]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | `string` | optional | "human" | "json". |
| `min_confidence` | `string` | optional | Suppress low-evidence findings ("high" | "all"). |

## Constraints

* `queue = "all"` rejects `cancel_running = true` at load —
  killing a run would silently drop a promised commit.
* `runner.kind` and `trigger.kind`/`status.kind` resolve to impl
  crates; unknown kinds fail at `mimus doctor`/startup.
* `deny_unknown_fields`: typos in field names fail the load.

---

---
url: /mimus/reference/violations.md
---
# Reference: violation format

`mimus check --format json` (and `mimus report --format json`)
emit a JSON array of violations — the contract anything
consuming mimus output (reconcile, CI annotations, dashboards)
should code against.

## Shape

```json
[
  {
    "claim": {
      "kind": "path",
      "text": "crates/old-crate/src/lib.rs",
      "source": "docs/guide.md",
      "line": 17
    },
    "evidence": "./crates/old-crate/src/lib.rs does not exist",
    "fix": "remove the reference, or restore the file",
    "severity": "error"
  }
]
```

## Fields

| field             | meaning                                            |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `claim.kind`      | `path` `command` `symbol` `count` `link` `behavior` |
| `claim.text`      | the claim as written in the source                  |
| `claim.source`    | file the claim was extracted from                   |
| `claim.line`      | 1-based line number                                 |
| `evidence`        | what reality says instead — the proof               |
| `fix`             | suggested correction, or `null`                     |
| `severity`        | `error` (gates `check`) | `warn` (report only)     |

## Human format

Default output is one line per violation:

```
docs/guide.md:17 [error] `crates/old-crate/src/lib.rs` — ./crates/old-crate/src/lib.rs does not exist
N violation(s)
```

`source:line [severity] `claim` — evidence` — stable enough to
grep, intended for terminals not parsers.

## Exit codes

| code | meaning                                         |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | clean — or `report`, which never gates          |
| 1    | `error`-severity violation(s), or usage failure |

`audit` always exits 0 — its scores are report-tier.

## What is silence, not a violation

mimus's rule is evidence-or-silence: a claim a checker cannot
prove false emits nothing. Concretely, none of these produce a
violation:

* `/leading-slash` spans — read as URL routes or host-absolute
  paths, never repo-relative claims
* `a/b`-shaped misses (`application/pdf`, `tools/list`) — two
  lowercase-word segments read as MIME types / RPC methods
* `VAR=value` env assignments, `...`-/brace-/`<>`-template
  spans, bare extensions (`.md`), serial placeholders
  (`adr-mkt-0N.md`)
* `~`- and `$`-prefixed paths, and globs verified by expansion
* command claims whose binary is declared in
  `[check].binaries`, or all command claims under `--no-cmd`

## Tuning and suppression

* `[check].kinds` / `[check].ignore_prefixes` / `base_dirs` —
  see [config](config.md)
* `<!-- mimus-ignore -->` — alone on a line, suppresses the next
  line's claims; inline, suppresses its own line.
  `<!-- mimus-ignore-file -->` skips the whole file.
* the `cmd` checker probes the machine's PATH — results vary
  across machines by design (missing binary = `warn`, never
  `error`). Declare prerequisites in `[check].binaries`, or run
  `check --no-cmd`.

# Explanation: architecture

mimus is the falsification half of the ecosystem: *"every claim
in your docs, comments, and memory — still true?"* It exists
because memory without doubt decays into confident confabulation.

## The pipeline

```
sources ──► extract ──► classify ──► verify ──► emit
   │          │           │           │          │
 docs/*.md  claims     kinds:     checkers:   human |
 comments   +lines     path…      fs cmd      json
 .kuda/                 behavior  symbol      exit 1
 cards                            rules
```

**Extract** pulls claim candidates (backticked spans, code
blocks, prose patterns) with source+line.

**Classify** sorts them into the taxonomy — conservatively: a
span that might be a command but isn't in the binary allowlist
is *not* a command claim.

**Verify** runs the mechanical checkers plus `rules/*.toml`.

**Emit** reports violations — or exits 1 to gate CI.

## Ports and adapters

`mimus-core` holds domain types only (`Claim`, `Violation`,
`TrustScore`, config). Every concern is a trait crate + adapter
crates:

* `mimus-check` (the checker port) → `mimus-check-fs`,
  `mimus-check-cmd`, `mimus-check-symbol` (against kuda's index)
* claim sources: markdown today, comments/cards wired in config
* `mimus-rules` — conventions as `rules/*.toml` data
* `mimus-vcs`→`mimus-git`, `mimus-config`→`mimus-config-toml`,
  `mimus-secret`→`mimus-keyring`/`mimus-dotenv`

A new checker = new adapter crate; a new convention = a new
rule file.

## The evidence bar

A violation is claim + evidence + suggested fix. No evidence,
no finding — false positives kill a critic faster than false
negatives. The semantic tier can never gate CI: it reports, a
human adjudicates. Style opinions are never emitted at all.

## Position in the ecosystem

* `kuda` builds the index; `mimus` doubts it — `audit`
  trust-scores cards against source via provenance hashes.
* `reconcile` (planned third tool) auto-fixes what mimus
  confirms: claims rewritten to match reality — it consumes the
  JSON violation contract, not the checkers.

See [claims & tiers](claims.md) for the taxonomy and why the
two tiers can never merge.

---

---
url: /mimus/explanation/claims.md
---
# Explanation: claims, tiers, and the evidence bar

mimus is built on one observation: documentation is full of
*claims* — statements that are either still true or quietly
false. A critic's job is to enumerate them and prove each one,
or stay silent.

## Claim taxonomy

Extraction classifies backticked spans, code blocks and prose
patterns into:

| kind      | example claim                        | verified by                |
| --------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| `path`    | `` `src/lib.rs` ``                   | filesystem                 |
| `command` | `` `cargo test -p foo` ``            | binary on PATH (no exec)   |
| `symbol`  | `` `IndexStore` ``                   | kuda index (symbol checker)|
| `count`   | "357 suites / 4,298 tests"           | recomputation              |
| `link`    | `[docs](https://…)`                  | link checker               |
| `behavior`| prose asserting code does X          | rules + semantic tier      |

Command claims are conservative by design: only spans whose
first token is a known binary (`cargo`, `git`, `npm`, `dagger`,
`kuda`, `mimus`, …) classify as commands — otherwise `pub fn`
and `data Eq` get read as shell.

## Verification tiers

* **Mechanical** — deterministic and offline: paths, commands,
  rules. This is the `mimus check` gate; if it flags something,
  the evidence is reproducible by anyone.
* **Semantic** — advisory: the `acp` checker spawns an ACP agent
  (`acp_cmd`, e.g. `env CLINE_PROVIDER=cline-pass
  CLINE_MODEL=cline-free/mimo-v2.6-flash cline --acp` —
  provider/model are env vars; -P/-m flags are ignored in ACP mode) to verify `behavior` claims —
  including kuda card prose. Runs with `--all` or
  `[check].semantic`; every finding is `warn` + evidence.
  **Can never gate** — that is load-bearing, not a limitation.
  Claims fold into one prompt per batch, and each prompt is
  debounced — polite to the provider.

Style opinions are never emitted at all.

## The evidence bar

Every violation is `claim + evidence + fix(optional)`. If a
checker cannot cite its proof, it emits nothing — false
positives kill a critic faster than false negatives ever could.
This is why `command` has an allowlist, why a bad rule regex is
silence + a doctor complaint, and why the semantic tier exists
separately from the gate.

## Sources

`[sources]` in `mimus.toml`: `docs` (glob list), `comments`
(code comments — TODOs, claims in `///`), and `cards` — the
kuda artifacts get audited as claims too, closing the loop:
kuda remembers, mimus doubts, even about the memory itself.

---

---
url: /mimus/explanation/release-model.md
---
# The release model

mimus releases itself — there is no hosted CI and no release tool
in the loop. Two deliberate phases:

## Phase 1 — the explicit seed

`mimus deploy release` runs once, by hand: it reads cargo metadata,
topologically orders the workspace's path-dependency graph,
`cargo publish`es every member, tags `{repo}-v{version}`, and pushes
the tag.

Why explicit? Publishing is the **only irreversible step** in the
whole system. Queues, runs, and statuses are all idempotent and
local; a crate version on crates.io is forever. Everything else in
mimus fires on push — the seed doesn't. (`--dry-run` prints the
order and tag without touching anything.)

## Phase 2 — push-driven forever after

From then on a release is *just another mimus job*: a push to `main`
hits the webhook, queues latest-wins, and runs `scripts/release.sh`
in a detached worktree under the shell runner.

The script:

1. diffs crate paths since the last `mimus-v*` tag
2. `cargo set-version --bump patch` on touched crates only (the cli
   republishes on any change — it's the install artifact)
3. `cargo publish`es them in dep order
4. tags `mimus-vX.Y.Z`, builds host-arch binaries with `cargo dist`,
   uploads to a GitHub Release via `gh`

The 5-minute sleep at the top isn't a hack — it's the debounce
window. Combined with `queue = "latest"` + `cancel_running`, rapid
push bursts collapse to one release of the newest sha; killed runs
get an honest "cancelled" status.

## Why this shape

* **No release-plz / GHA**: the point of the project is that CI is a
  local loop — depending on hosted CI to ship it would be
  self-defeating. `scripts/release.sh` is deliberately boring bash so it can
  run as a plain `cmd` under `runner.kind = "shell"`.
* **Latest-wins, not `all`**: a release that misses an intermediate
  push loses nothing — the tag lands on HEAD, which contains
  everything. `queue = "all"` is for pipelines where each sha's run
  is individually meaningful.
* **Explicit over automatic**: a wrong tag or half-published
  workspace is far worse than a delayed release; the boundary sits
  exactly at irreversibility.

Host prerequisites: `cargo-edit`, `cargo-dist`, `gh`, and
`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (env → keyring → env file). Multi-arch
binaries arrive when the remote-runner pair lands — see TODO.

---

---
url: /mimus/comparison.md
---
# mimus vs the alternatives

## vs linters

|                     | linters              | mimus                       |
| ------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| checks              | code shape           | claims about reality          |
| docs                | mostly ignored       | first-class source            |
| output              | style/correctness    | claim + evidence + fix        |
| rules               | per-language config  | `rules/*.toml`, evidence-bound|

They complement each other — a linter says the code is shaped
right; mimus says the docs tell the truth.

## vs LLM doc review

|                     | "review the docs" prompt | mimus                    |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| coverage            | broad, vague             | only what's checkable      |
| false positives     | high                     | evidence-or-silence        |
| CI gate             | unsafe                   | mechanical tier is safe    |
| cost                | per-run                  | mechanical tier is free    |

The LLM still has a role — as the `check-llm` adapter for the
semantic tier, where findings are advisory by design.

## vs doctest-style tools

|                     | doctests/link-checkers | mimus                       |
| ------------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| scope               | code blocks only       | all factual prose             |
| claim types         | one or two             | path/cmd/symbol/count/link    |
| memory audit        | n/a                    | `.kuda/` card trust scores    |

---

---
url: /mimus/getting-started.md
---
# Getting started

Pick by what you need to do.

* **Tutorials** (learn): [first-run](tutorials/first-run.md)
* **How-to** (tasks): [memory audit](how-to/kuda-audit.md) ·
  [rules authoring](how-to/rules-authoring.md)
* **Reference** (lookup): [cli](reference/cli.md) ·
  [config](reference/config.md) ·
  [crate api](reference/crate-api.md)
* **Explanation** (why): [architecture](explanation/architecture.md) ·
  [release model](explanation/release-model.md) ·
  [comparison](comparison.md) — vs linters / LLM review

Install:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/mimus mimus
```

First check:

```sh
cd your-repo
mimus init    # detect claim sources -> mimus.toml + rules/
mimus check   # mechanical tier: paths, commands, symbols
mimus report  # violations with claim + evidence + fix
```

`symbol` claims, `audit`, and `coverage` need a
[kuda](https://github.com/9aia/kuda) index (`kuda sync`) — without
one, the mechanical tier is paths + commands + rules.
